prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Houston for AC repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” HVAC company for every Houston customer — the right choice depends on your ZIP code, what’s wrong (simple repair vs. major replacement), your budget, and whether you need emergency service. I can help narrow it down if you tell me your ZIP code and whether this is an emergency.

To get you started, here’s a quick, practical plan and a short list of things to check when choosing an AC repair company:

What to check
- Local reputation: Google Reviews, Yelp, Angi, and Better Business Bureau. Look for many recent, detailed reviews (not just star ratings).
- Licensing and certifications: technicians should have EPA 608 certification for refrigerant work and the contractor should be registered with Texas (check TDLR or the state site for complaints/registration).
- Insurance: ask for proof of liability insurance and worker’s comp.
- Experience with your brand/model: make sure they’ve worked on your AC make.
- Clear pricing: get a written estimate that lists parts, labor, and diagnostic fees. Ask whether quotes are flat-rate or hourly.
- Warranties/guarantees: ask about parts and workmanship warranties and how long they last.
- Emergency availability & response time: if you need same-day or after-hours service, confirm their policy and fees.
- References: for major jobs, ask for local references or photos of past similar work.

Questions to ask when you call
- Are you licensed/registered in Texas and insured?
- Do your techs have EPA 608 and NATE (or other) certifications?
- What is the diagnostic fee, and does it apply to the repair?
- What is your service call window and emergency policy?
- Do you offer any warranties/guarantees on repairs?
- Can you give a written estimate?

Names to consider (examples, not an exhaustive ranking)
- John Moore Services — long-established Houston company with broad local service.
- ARS/Rescue Rooter and Service Experts — national brands with Houston branches; often have quick response and standard policies.
- Local independent contractors — often cheaper and responsive for neighborhood repairs; pick one with strong recent local reviews and proper licensing.

If you want, give me:
- your ZIP code,
- whether it’s an emergency,
- AC brand/model (if known),
and I’ll give a short, customized list of well-reviewed companies near you and a suggested next step.
